newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea again warns U.S. over submarine row.
newsitem.headline: North Korea again warns U.S. over submarine row.

text.p: North Korea again warned the United States on Friday not to side with South Korea in a row over a North Korean submarine that ran aground in the South in September.

The state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), in a report seen in Tokyo, also accused South Korea of trying to scuttle work by the Korean Energy Development Organisation (KEDO) to overhaul North Korea's nuclear reactors.

"The South Korean puppets, who persistently stood against the adoption of the DPRK (North Korea)-U.S. framework agreement from the beginning, are trying to lay an obstacle in the way of KEDO's supplying LWRs (Light Water Reactors) to the DPRK by fabricating a 'Spyship Intrusion Case' recently," KCNA said.
"The United States, which is in the leading position of the KEDO, is encouraging the puppets and siding with them.
"We do not care about whether the provision of LWR is delayed and whether the KEDO is dissolved. But we will act according to our independent right," KCNA added.

Under a 1994 agreement between the United States and North Korea, KEDO is to replace North Korea's plutonium-breeding reactors with light-water reactors in exchange for a freeze on Pyongyang's nuclear programme.
Tension has remained high on the divided Korean Peninsula, since a submarine landed 26 North Koreans in September off South Korea's eastern city of Kangnung.
Twenty-four of the intruders have been shot dead, one was captured and the other is still missing.
Earlier this month, North Korea warned the United States that the nuclear pact could be jeopardised by Washington's stance on the submarine incident.
Seoul, which had pledged to foot most of the $5 billion cost of building nuclear plants for the communist state, has hinted it might withdraw its backing for the nuclear accord.
South Korea has demanded Pyongyang apologise for the submarine incident but North Korea has instead demanded the return of the vessel, the captured crewmember and the bodies of the dead crew.
KCNA's warnings came two days after North Korea released American Carl Hunziker, who had been detained in the communist state for three months on espionage charges.
The two Koreas technically remain at war since the 1950-53 Korean War ended without a peace agreement.
